source_excerpt: Unless otherwise provided by the policy, when a homeowner’s insurance policy provides for adjustment and settlement of first-party losses based on repair or replacement cost, covered physical damage incurred in making repair or replacement is included within applicable limits; when replacement items do not match in quality, color, or size, the insurer shall make reasonable repairs or replacement in adjoining areas, considering relevant factors including cost, uniformity, and remaining useful life.

For an extracontractual property-insurance claim, the statute requires an adverse adjudication establishing breach and a final judgment or decree; payment of an appraisal award is not an adverse adjudication and does not alone create a cause of action.

The current statute addresses acknowledgment within 7 calendar days, prompt investigation after proof-of-loss statements, a 30-day physical-inspection period, detailed-estimate delivery, and payment-or-denial within 60 days subject to statutory exceptions and tolling.

The unfair-claim-settlement-practices provision addresses material misrepresentation and specified practices, including failure to adopt proper investigation standards, misrepresentation of pertinent facts or policy provisions, failure to act promptly on communications, and denial without reasonable investigation, when performed with sufficient frequency to indicate a general business practice.
